brief_summary: Three-row ladder of cantilever tabs fixed to a case wall at the left, each loaded at the free end. Tab stroke weight and deflection scale with thickness (1.0 mm, 1.5 mm, 2.0 mm). Beside each tab a bordeaux bar shows relative spring rate: 1x, 3.4x, 8x — the cube of thickness. A footnote states the proportionality (E · b · t³ / L³) and that a longer tab is softer by the cube of length.
data_sources: leaf-spring-mount-deep-dive.mdx § 'A tab that bends on purpose' — 'the spring rate of the tab rises with the cube of its thickness, rises linearly with its width and the material's modulus, and falls with the cube of its length'

leaf-spring-mount-deep-dive.mdx § 'A tab that bends on purpose' — 'A 1.0 mm tab and a 1.5 mm tab in the same alloy and the same length differ in stiffness by a factor of about 3.4. A 2.0 mm tab is eight times stiffer than the 1.0 mm one.'
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deflection_(engineering) — cantilever end-load deflection δ = P·L³ / (3·E·I), with I = b·t³/12 for a rectangular section
